_comment: A chain: problems that fill the same table, ordered so each one is one change from an earlier one. Solve them in order, in one sitting, to see the change. diag = dp[i-1][j-1], up = dp[i-1][j], left = dp[i][j-1]; a, b = the current characters x[i-1], y[j-1]. Drafted 2026-09-23 from the cached solutions; 583 uses the direct deletion table, 516 and 1312 use s against s[::-1].

583.title: Delete Operation for Two Strings
583.change: count what you drop instead of what you keep

712.title: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings
712.change: a deletion costs ord(c) instead of 1

1092.title: Shortest Common Supersequence
1092.answer: walk back from the corner, build the string
1092.change: return the string, not the number

1312.title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make a String Palindrome
1312.change: 583 on s and s[::-1]: count what you add instead of what you keep

115.title: Distinct Subsequences
115.change: count ways (sum), and only s may drop characters

1458.title: Max Dot Product of Two Subsequences
1458.change: a match scores a product, the result can't be empty

97.title: Interleaving String
97.match: (up and a == c) or (left and b == c), c = s3[i+j-1]
97.change: bool table, a third string gives the target character

10.title: Regular Expression Matching
10.mismatch: *: two columns left, or up if the character before * matches
